text: The one breaking change this week is #10520: the blocked customer check event on table Customer now passes the extensible Gen. Journal Document Type enum value instead of an option integer, so subscribers need review. Most other work was behaviour fixes in BCApps. Direct transfer upgrade failures without Inventory Setup were fixed in #12907 and #12939. Posting and costing fixes include #12816 (project planning line order), #11714 (assembly cost adjustment rounding), #10500 (additional-currency cost on project ledger entries) and #11757 (Spanish payment orders). Sales and purchasing fixes cover #12806 (partial orders after closing the browser during quote conversion), #12469 (manual direct unit costs kept in carry out), #12809 and #12551. Planning fixes are #12464 and #12760, where a blocked item no longer stops Order Planning, and #12669 and #12459 for subcontracting dates and prices. Subscription Billing received #12857, #12622 and #12377. Agent work includes #11909, which blocks guest users from managing Expense Agent, #12817 and #9359 for Sales Order Agent, and Expense Agent VAT setup fixes #12810 and #12472. E-documents changes are #12148 for PEPPOL Order Response, #12575 and #11527. Fabric mirroring raised its table limit to 1000 in #12565 and gained a table reset in #12339. Extensibility additions are #11580 and #10523. Smaller refactors moved HTTP and URL checks to native modules in #12614, #12755 and #12617.

issues: Several pull requests are named with no description (#12809, #12551, #12857, #12622, #12377, #12575, #11527, #11580, #10523), so readers learn only which area they belong to. A short clause each would help, for example #12809 (a vendor change on one purchase order no longer carries over to the next order) and #12622 (contract currency is kept on generated invoices).
'native modules' is loose wording. #12614 and #12755 moved to native HttpClient, while #12617 moved URL checks to the System Application Uri module.
The paragraph is about 213 words, close to the 220-word limit.
